tips: Trap is A 'state-of-the-art technology' — tactical concern, not strategic.
Trap is B 'operational controls' — implementation detail, not strategic.
Trap is D 'project management practices' — process detail, not strategic content.
IT mission and vision = the strategic anchor. Without them articulated, the strategic plan has no narrative for what IT exists to do.

questions.question: A small organization has only one database administrator (DBA) and one system administrator. The DBA has root access to the UNIX server, which hosts the database application. How should separation of duties be enforced in this scenario?

options.A: Hire a second DBA and split the duties between the two individuals.
options.B: Remove the DBA's root access on all UNIX servers.
options.C: Ensure that all actions of the DBA are logged and that all logs are backed up to removable media.
options.D: Ensure that database logs are forwarded to a UNIX server where the DBA does not have root access.

questions.correct_explanation: By creating logs that the DBA cannot erase or modify, separation of duties is enforced.

wrong_explanations.A: Hiring additional staff is a costly way to ensure separation of duties.
wrong_explanations.B: The database administrator (DBA) needs root access to the database servers to install upgrades or patches.
wrong_explanations.C: The administrator can modify or erase logs prior to the media backup event.

tips: Trap is A 'hire a second DBA' — small org constraint makes this impractical.
Trap is B 'remove DBA root access' — would prevent the DBA from doing their job.
Trap is C 'log to removable media' — DBA could intercept or alter the media.
Forwarding logs to a server the DBA can't access creates a tamper-evident record. SoD is enforced through inability to cover one's tracks.

questions.question: Which of the following user profiles should be of MOST concern to an information systems (IS) auditor when performing an audit of an electronic funds transfer system?

options.A: Three users with the ability to capture and verify their own messages
options.B: Five users with the ability to capture and send their own messages
options.C: Five users with the ability to verify other users and to send their own messages
options.D: Three users with the ability to capture and verify the messages of other users and to send their own messages

questions.correct_explanation: The ability of one individual to capture and verify their own messages represents an inadequate segregation because messages can be taken as correct and appear like they had already been verified. The verification of messages should not be allowed by the person who sent the message.

wrong_explanations.B: Users may have the ability to send messages but should not be able to verify their own messages.
wrong_explanations.C: This profile is an example of separation of duties. A person can send their own message but only verify the messages of other users.
wrong_explanations.D: The ability to capture and verify the messages of others but only send their own messages is acceptable.

tips: Capture + verify by the same user = no segregation. The verifier has no independent perspective.
Trap is B 'capture and send' — separate function from verification; legitimate role combination.
Trap is C 'verify others + send own' — verification is independent of own messages; acceptable.
Trap is D 'capture and verify others' messages, send own' — verifying OTHERS' messages is independent oversight; acceptable. Self-verification (option A) is the SoD violation.

questions.question: Which of the following does an information systems (IS) auditor FIRST reference when performing an IS audit?

options.A: Implemented procedures
options.B: Approved policies
options.C: Internal standards
options.D: Documented practices

questions.correct_explanation: Policies are high-level documents that represent the corporate philosophy of an organization. Internal standards, procedures and practices are subordinate to policy.

wrong_explanations.A: Procedures are implemented in accordance with policy.
wrong_explanations.C: Standards are subordinate to policy.
wrong_explanations.D: Practices are subordinate to policy.

tips: Trap is A 'implemented procedures' — derive from policy, not the reference point.
Trap is C 'internal standards' — also subordinate to policy.
Trap is D 'documented practices' — describe what's happening, not the authority.
Hierarchy: policy (top) → standard → procedure → practice (bottom). Audit always starts at the top — the authoritative document — and works down.

questions.question: An enterprise selected a vendor to develop and implement a new software system. To ensure that the enterprise's investment in software is protected, which of the following security clauses is MOST important to include in the master services agreement?

options.A: Limitation of liability
options.B: Service level requirements
options.C: Software escrow
options.D: Version control

questions.correct_explanation: Software escrow clauses in a contract ensure that the software source code will still be available to the organization in the event of a vendor issue, such as insolvency and copyright issues.

wrong_explanations.A: A limitation of liability clause protects the financial exposure of the organization but not its software investment.
wrong_explanations.B: Service level requirements specify financial penalties for not meeting standards, but these do not address issues of vendor insolvency.
wrong_explanations.D: Version control is related to the software development life cycle and not the software investment.

tips: Trap is A 'limitation of liability' — contract/legal protection, not investment protection.
Trap is B 'service level requirements' — performance protection, not asset protection.
Trap is D 'version control' — operational practice, not contractual safeguard.
Software escrow protects the long-term investment: if the vendor disappears, the customer can still maintain and modify the software. Critical for enterprise systems.

questions.question: When implementing an IT governance framework in an organization, the MOST important objective is:

options.A: IT alignment with the business.
options.B: accountability.
options.C: value realization with IT.
options.D: enhancing the return on IT investments.

questions.correct_explanation: The goals of IT governance are to improve IT performance, deliver optimum business value and ensure regulatory compliance. The key practice in support of these goals is the strategic alignment of IT with the business. To achieve alignment, all other choices need to be tied to business practices and strategies.

wrong_explanations.B: Accountability is important, but the most important objective of IT governance is to ensure that IT investment and oversight are aligned with business requirements.
wrong_explanations.C: IT must demonstrate value to the organization, but this value is dependent on the ability of IT to align with, and support, business requirements.
wrong_explanations.D: Enhancing return is a requirement of the IT governance framework, but this requirement is only demonstrated through aligning IT with business requirements.

tips: Trap is B 'accountability' — necessary supporting practice, not the most important objective.
Trap is C 'value realization' — outcome of governance, follows from alignment.
Trap is D 'enhancing ROI' — financial outcome, follows from alignment.
IT governance's most important objective: aligning IT with business. Everything else (accountability, value, ROI) flows from that alignment.

questions.question: Measures of security risk should:

options.A: address all of the network risk.
options.B: be tracked over time against the IT strategic plan.
options.C: consider the entire IT environment.
options.D: result in the identification of vulnerability tolerances.

questions.correct_explanation: When assessing IT security risk, it is important to consider the entire IT environment.

wrong_explanations.A: Measures of security risk should not be limited to network risk, but rather focus on those areas with the highest criticality so that maximum risk reduction is achieved at the lowest possible cost.
wrong_explanations.B: IT strategic plans are not granular enough to provide appropriate measures. Objective metrics must be tracked over time against measurable goals; thus, the management of risk is enhanced by comparing today's results against results from last week, last month and last quarter. Risk measures will profile assets on a network to objectively measure vulnerability risk.
wrong_explanations.D: Measures of security risk do not identify tolerances.

tips: Trap is A 'all network risk' — too narrow; risk extends beyond network to applications, data, users, processes.
Trap is B 'tracked over time against IT strategic plan' — useful but secondary to comprehensive coverage.
Trap is D 'identify vulnerability tolerances' — outcome of measurement, not the measurement itself.
Security risk measurement must be COMPREHENSIVE — the entire IT environment, not subsets. Partial coverage = blind spots.

questions.question: The ultimate purpose of IT governance is to:

options.A: encourage optimal use of IT.
options.B: reduce IT costs.
options.C: decentralize IT resources across the organization.
options.D: centralize control of IT.

questions.correct_explanation: The purpose of IT governance is to direct the IT endeavors to ensure that IT performance meets the objectives of aligning IT with the enterprise's objectives and the realization of promised benefits. Thus, generating business value and mitigating the risks associated with IT, results in the optimal use of IT.

wrong_explanations.B: Reducing IT costs may not be the best IT governance outcome for an enterprise.
wrong_explanations.C: Decentralizing IT resources across the organization is not always desired, although it may be desired in a decentralized environment.
wrong_explanations.D: Centralizing control of IT is not always desired. An example of where it might be desired is an enterprise wanting a single point of customer contact.

tips: Trap is B 'reduce IT costs' — possible outcome, not the ultimate purpose.
Trap is C/D 'decentralize / centralize control' — structural choices, both can be valid; not the purpose.
IT governance's ULTIMATE purpose: getting OPTIMAL value from IT, where optimal = aligned with business strategy + reasonable cost + managed risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important for an information systems (IS) auditor to consider when reviewing a service level agreement with an external IT service provider?

options.A: Payment terms
options.B: Uptime guarantee
options.C: Indemnification clause
options.D: Default resolution

questions.correct_explanation: The most important element of an SLA is the measurable terms of performance, such as uptime agreements.

wrong_explanations.A: Payment terms are typically included in the master agreement rather than in the service level agreement (SLA).
wrong_explanations.C: The indemnification clause is typically included in the master agreement rather than in the SLA.
wrong_explanations.D: The default resolution only applies in case of a default of the SLA; therefore, it is more important to review the performance conditions of the SLA.

tips: Trap is A 'payment terms' — typically in master agreement, not SLA.
Trap is C 'indemnification' — legal protection, not service measurement.
Trap is D 'default resolution' — applies after default, doesn't ensure performance.
SLA's central element: measurable performance commitments. Uptime is the most universal measurable performance term and represents the SLA's core value.

questions.question: The PRIMARY objective of implementing corporate governance is to:

options.A: provide strategic direction.
options.B: control business operations.
options.C: align IT with business.
options.D: implement good practices.

questions.correct_explanation: Corporate governance is a set of management practices to provide strategic direction to the organization as a whole, thereby ensuring that goals are achievable, risk is properly addressed and organizational resources are properly used. Hence, the primary objective of corporate governance is to provide strategic direction. B.Business operations are directed and controlled based on the strategic direction.

wrong_explanations.C: Corporate governance applies strategic planning, monitoring and accountability to the entire organization, not just to lT.
wrong_explanations.D: Governance is applied through the use of good practices, but this is not the objective of corporate governance.

tips: Trap is B 'control business operations' — too operational; that's management's job.
Trap is C 'align IT with business' — that's IT governance, a SUBSET of corporate governance.
Trap is D 'implement good practices' — outcome of governance, not the primary objective.
Corporate governance = strategic direction-setting at the enterprise level. IT alignment is one of many governance concerns; strategic direction is the umbrella.

questions.question: Which of the following should be considered FIRST when implementing a risk management program?

options.A: An understanding of the organization's threat, vulnerability and risk profile
options.B: An understanding of the risk exposures and the potential consequences of compromise
options.C: A determination of risk management priorities that are based on potential consequences
options.D: A risk mitigation strategy sufficient to keep risk consequences at an acceptable level

questions.correct_explanation: Implementing risk management-one of the outcomes of effective information security governance -requires a collective understanding of the organization's threat, vulnerability and risk profile as a first step.

wrong_explanations.B: An understanding of risk exposure and potential consequences of compromise can be determined only after there is an understanding of the organization's threat, vulnerability and risk profile.
wrong_explanations.C: Risk management priorities that are based on potential consequences (the magnitude of the impact) and the probability of occurrence can only be developed after the organization's threat, vulnerability and risk profile is determined and evaluated.
wrong_explanations.D: Risk mitigation priorities are based on the risk profile, risk acceptance levels and potential mitigating controls. These elements provide a basis for the formulation of strategies for risk mitigation sufficient to keep the consequences from risk at an acceptable level. This forms part of the last step in the risk assessment process.

tips: Trap is B 'understand exposures and consequences' — comes AFTER understanding the threat/vulnerability/risk profile.
Trap is C 'determine priorities based on consequences' — also comes after.
Trap is D 'risk mitigation strategy' — final step, can't be designed without first understanding the risk landscape.
Risk management starts with understanding what risks the org faces. Threat/vulnerability/risk profile is the foundation; everything else builds on it.

questions.question: In the context of effective information security governance, the PRIMARY objective of value delivery is to:

options.A: optimize security investments in support of business objectives.
options.B: implement a standard set of security practices.
options.C: institute a standards-based solution.
options.D: implement a continuous improvement culture.

questions.correct_explanation: Information security governance provides strategic direction for security activities and ensures that business objectives are achieved. Therefore, in the context of effective information security governance, value delivery is implemented to ensure optimization of security investments in support of business objectives.

wrong_explanations.B: The tools and techniques for implementing value delivery include implementation of a standard set of security practices; however, implementation of standards is a means to achieve the objective of supporting value delivery, not the objective itself.
wrong_explanations.C: Value delivery may be supported with standards-based solutions, but the use of standards-based solutions is not the goal of value delivery.
wrong_explanations.D: Continuous improvement culture in relation to a security program is a process, not an objective.

tips: Trap is B 'standard set of practices' — implementation tactic, not the value-delivery objective.
Trap is C 'standards-based solution' — same; tactic.
Trap is D 'continuous improvement culture' — process orientation, not the value objective.
Value delivery in security governance: optimize security spend so it actively SUPPORTS business objectives (not just minimizes risk in isolation).

questions.question: A driver of IT governance, transparency of IT cost, value and risk is primarily achieved through:

options.A: performance measurement.
options.B: strategic alignment.
options.C: value delivery.
options.D: resource management.

questions.correct_explanation: Performance measurement includes setting and monitoring measurable objectives that the IT processes need to achieve to deliver (process outcome), and how they deliver it (process capability and performance). Transparency is primarily achieved through performance measurement because it provides information to the stakeholders on how well the enterprise is performing when compared to objectives.

wrong_explanations.B: Strategic alignment primarily focuses on ensuring linkage of business and IT plans, not on transparency.
wrong_explanations.C: Value delivery is about executing the value proposition throughout the delivery cycle. Value delivery ensures that IT investments deliver on promised values but does not ensure transparency of investment.
wrong_explanations.D: Resource management is about the optimal investment in and proper management of critical IT resources but does not ensure transparency of IT investments.

tips: Trap is B 'strategic alignment' — connects IT to business but doesn't itself create transparency.
Trap is C 'value delivery' — execution of strategy, doesn't create transparency about cost/value/risk.
Trap is D 'resource management' — optimizes resources, doesn't measure cost/value/risk for stakeholders.
Performance measurement = transparency. KPIs and metrics make the cost/value/risk picture visible to stakeholders. That's how transparency is achieved.

questions.question: Which of the following should be the MOST important consideration when deciding on areas of priority for IT governance implementations?

options.A: Process maturity
options.B: Performance indicators
options.C: Business risk
options.D: Assurance reports

questions.correct_explanation: Priority should be given to those business areas of the enterprise operations that face real risk based on the probability of occurrence and the magnitude of the impact.

wrong_explanations.A: The level of process maturity evolves as the implementation of the IT governance program occurs and may feed into the decision-making process. Those areas that represent real risk to the business should be given priority.
wrong_explanations.B: The level of process performance demonstrates the effectiveness of the program but is not the means to establish priorities for governance. Those areas that represent real risk to the business should be given priority.
wrong_explanations.D: Assurance (audit) reports provide assurance of the effectiveness of the implementation of governance but do not determine the priorities for a program. Those areas that represent real risk to the business should be given priority.

tips: Trap is A 'process maturity' — useful input but not the priority driver.
Trap is B 'performance indicators' — measurement framework, not priority driver.
Trap is D 'assurance reports' — historical view, not forward priority driver.
Business risk drives governance priorities. High-risk areas get governance attention first; low-risk areas can wait.

questions.question: Responsibility for the governance of IT should rest with the:

options.A: IT strategy committee.
options.B: chief information officer (CIO).
options.C: audit committee.
options.D: board of directors.

questions.correct_explanation: Governance is the set of responsibilities and practices exercised by the board and executive management with the goal of providing strategic direction, ensuring that objectives are achieved, ascertaining that risk is managed appropriately and verifying that the enterprise's resources are used responsibly.

wrong_explanations.A: The IT strategy committee plays a significant role in the successful implementation of IT governance within an organization, but the ultimate responsibility resides with the board of directors.
wrong_explanations.B: The chief information officer (CIO) plays a significant role in the successful implementation of IT governance within an organization, but the ultimate responsibility resides with the board of directors.
wrong_explanations.C: The audit committee plays a significant role in monitoring and overseeing the successful implementation of IT governance within an organization, but the ultimate responsibility resides with the board of directors.

tips: Trap is A 'IT strategy committee' — supports board-level governance, doesn't own it.
Trap is B 'CIO' — implements governance set by board, doesn't own ultimate responsibility.
Trap is C 'audit committee' — oversees audit function specifically, not all of IT governance.
Board of directors owns enterprise governance, including IT governance. They delegate execution but retain accountability.

questions.question: Which of the following is normally a responsibility of the chief information security officer (CISO)?

options.A: Periodically reviewing and evaluating the security policy
options.B: Executing user application and software testing and evaluation
options.C: Granting and revoking user access to IT resources
options.D: Approving access to data and applications

questions.correct_explanation: The role of the chief information security officer (CISO) is to ensure that the corporate security policy and controls are adequate to prevent unauthorized access to the enterprise assets, including data, programs and equipment.

wrong_explanations.B: User application and other software testing and evaluation normally are the responsibility of the staff assigned to development and maintenance.
wrong_explanations.C: Granting and revoking access to IT resources is usually a function of system, network or database administrators.
wrong_explanations.D: Approval of access to data and applications is the duty of the data or application owner.

tips: Trap is B 'execute software testing' — operational task, not CISO domain.
Trap is C 'granting/revoking user access' — sysadmin/IAM domain, not CISO.
Trap is D 'approving access to data and applications' — data owner / business owner, not CISO.
CISO's role: ensure security policy and controls are adequate. Periodic policy review and evaluation is core to that responsibility.

questions.question: When developing a formal enterprise security program, the MOST critical success factor (CSF) is the:

options.A: establishment of a review board.
options.B: creation of a security unit.
options.C: effective support of an executive sponsor.
options.D: selection of a security process owner.

questions.correct_explanation: The executive sponsor is in charge of supporting the organization's strategic security program and aids in directing the organization's overall security management activities. Therefore, support by the executive level of management is the most critical success factor (CSF).

wrong_explanations.A: Establishment of a review board is not effective without visible sponsorship of top management.
wrong_explanations.B: The creation of a security unit is not effective without visible sponsorship of top management.
wrong_explanations.D: The selection of a security process owner is not effective without visible sponsorship of top management.

tips: Trap is A/B 'review board / security unit' — structural elements, useful but not the most critical success factor.
Trap is D 'security process owner' — operational role, important but downstream of executive sponsorship.
Executive sponsorship is the make-or-break factor. With it, resources flow and obstacles clear; without it, the program stalls regardless of structure.

questions.question: When reviewing an organization's strategic IT plan, an information systems (IS) auditor should expect to find:

options.A: an assessment of the fit of the organization's application portfolio with business objectives.
options.B: actions to reduce hardware procurement cost.
options.C: a listing of approved suppliers of IT contract resources.
options.D: a description of the technical architecture for the organization's network perimeter security.

questions.correct_explanation: An assessment of how well an organization's application portfolio supports the organization's business objectives is a key component of the overall IT strategic planning process. This assessment drives the demand side of IT planning and should convert into a set of strategic IT intentions. Further assessment can then be made of how well the overall IT organization, encompassing applications, infrastructure, services, management processes, etc. can support the business objectives. The purpose of an IT strategic plan is to set out how IT will be used to achieve or support an organization's business objectives.

wrong_explanations.B: Operational efficiency initiatives, including cost reduction of purchasing and maintenance activities of systems, belong to tactical planning, not strategic planning.
wrong_explanations.C: A list of approved suppliers of IT contract resources is a tactical, rather than a strategic, concern.
wrong_explanations.D: An IT strategic plan does not normally include detail of a specific technical architecture.

tips: Trap is B/C 'reduce hardware cost / approved suppliers list' — operational/procurement detail, not strategic content.
Trap is D 'technical architecture for perimeter security' — too granular for strategic plan.
Strategic IT plan content: assessment of the application portfolio's fit with business objectives. That's the strategic question — does our tech support our business?

questions.question: When developing a security architecture, which of the following steps should be executed FIRST?

options.A: Developing security procedures
options.B: Defining a security policy
options.C: Specifying an access control methodology
options.D: Defining roles and responsibilities

questions.correct_explanation: Defining a security policy for information and related technology is the first step toward building a security architecture. A security policy communicates a coherent security standard to users, management and technical staff. Security policies often set the stage in terms of the tools and procedures that are needed for an organization.

wrong_explanations.A: Policy is used to provide direction for procedures, standards and baselines. Therefore, developing security procedures should be executed only after defining a security policy.
wrong_explanations.C: Specifying an access control methodology is an implementation concern and should be executed only after defining a security policy.
wrong_explanations.D: Defining roles and responsibilities should be executed only after defining a security policy.

tips: Trap is A 'developing security procedures' — derive from policy, not vice versa.
Trap is C 'access control methodology' — implementation detail, downstream of policy.
Trap is D 'roles and responsibilities' — derive from policy framework.
Security architecture cascade: policy → architecture → procedures → controls. Policy is the foundation; everything else flows from it.

questions.question: Which of the following should an information systems (IS) auditor recommend to BEST enforce alignment of an IT project portfolio with strategic organizational priorities?

options.A: Define a balanced scorecard (BSC) for measuring performance.
options.B: Consider user satisfaction in the key performance indicators (KPis).
options.C: Select projects according to business benefits and risk.
options.D: Modify the yearly process of defining the project portfolio.

questions.correct_explanation: Prioritization of projects on the basis of their expected benefit(s) to business, and the related risk, is the best measure for achieving alignment of the project portfolio to an organization's strategic priorities.

wrong_explanations.A: Measures such as a balanced scorecard (BSC) are helpful, but do not guarantee that the projects are aligned with business strategy.
wrong_explanations.B: Key performance indicators (KPls) are helpful to monitor and measure IT performance, but they do not guarantee that the projects are aligned with business strategy.
wrong_explanations.D: Modifying the yearly process of the project portfolio definition might improve the situation, but only if the portfolio definition process is closely tied to organizational strategies.

tips: Trap is A 'BSC for performance' — measurement framework, doesn't drive selection.
Trap is B 'user satisfaction in KPIs' — one dimension, not the selection driver.
Trap is D 'modify yearly process' — process change without principle change is insufficient.
Project portfolio alignment = selecting based on business benefit + risk. That's what ties projects to strategic priorities. Other practices support but don't drive selection.

questions.question: The PRIMARY benefit of implementing a security program as part of a security governance framework is the:

options.A: alignment of the IT activities with information systems (IS) audit recommendations.
options.B: enforcement of the management of security risk.
options.C: implementation of the chief information security officer's recommendations.
options.D: reduction of the cost for IT security.

questions.correct_explanation: The primary benefit of implementing a security program is management's assessment of risk and its mitigation to an appropriate level, and monitoring of the residual risk.

wrong_explanations.A: Recommendations of the information systems (IS) auditor are usually addressed as value addition within a security program, but that would not be the primary benefit of implementing a security program.
wrong_explanations.C: Recommendations and input of the chief information security officer are usually included within a security program, but that would not be the primary benefit of implementing a security program as part of a security governance framework.
wrong_explanations.D: The impact of the implementation of a security program on the cost of IT security is uncertain. It may or may not be reduced.

tips: Trap is A 'alignment with audit recommendations' — audit recommendations are inputs, not the security program's purpose.
Trap is C 'CISO recommendations implemented' — CISO advises; the program EXECUTES management's risk decisions.
Trap is D 'reduce IT security cost' — possible outcome but not the primary benefit.
Security program's primary benefit in governance: management actively manages security risk — assessing, mitigating, monitoring residual risk. That's risk governance in action.

questions.question: An organization has a well-established risk management process. Which of the following risk management practices would MOST likely expose the organization to the greatest amount of compliance risk?

options.A: Risk reduction
options.B: Risk transfer
options.C: Risk avoidance
options.D: Risk mitigation

questions.correct_explanation: Risk transfer spreads the risk by either transferring some or all of it to a third party ( e.g., through insurance or outsourcing) or applying the resources of multiple teams to hedge against possible losses. Risk transfer typically addresses financial risk and does not always address compliance risk.

wrong_explanations.A: Risk reduction is a term synonymous with risk mitigation. Risk reduction treats the risk, including compliance risk and lowers it to a level commensurate with the organization's risk appetite.
wrong_explanations.C: Risk avoidance does not expose the organization to compliance risk because the business practice that caused the inherent risk to exist is no longer being pursued or is eliminated altogether.
wrong_explanations.D: mitigating risk will still expose the organization to a certain amount of risk, risk mitigation lowers risk, including compliance risk, to a level commensurate with the organization's risk appetite.

tips: Trap is A/D 'risk reduction / risk mitigation' — both lower risk including compliance risk.
Trap is C 'risk avoidance' — eliminates the activity creating the risk, including compliance exposure.

Risk transfer (insurance, outsourcing) typically addresses FINANCIAL risk but doesn't transfer COMPLIANCE risk — regulators still hold the original org responsible for compliance regardless of who operates the function.

questions.question: An employee who has access to highly confidential information resigned. Upon departure, which of the following should be done FIRST?

options.A: Conduct an exit interview with the employee.
options.B: Ensure succession plans are in place.
options.C: Revoke the employee's access to all systems.
options.D: Review the employee's job history.

questions.correct_explanation: If an employee has dealt with highly classified information, the first step is to revoke their access to all systems, to restrict access to the confidential information and thereby prevent exfiltration of data.

wrong_explanations.A: It is important to have an exit interview with any employee; however, this is not the first step to take upon the employee's departure to protect the confidentiality of information.
wrong_explanations.B: Succession plans are important to prevent disruption of operations. This addresses availability and not confidentiality of information.
wrong_explanations.D: Reviewing the job history of an employee might be important to determine the functions the person performed, but its effectiveness in terms of confidentiality of information may be limited.

tips: Same as d2_032: when an employee with sensitive access leaves, REVOKE ACCESS FIRST. Time-critical to prevent exfiltration.
Trap is A 'exit interview' — important but can wait.
Trap is B 'succession plans' — operational continuity, not security urgency.
Trap is D 'review job history' — useful for context, not time-critical.

questions.question: An organization has outsourced its help desk activities. An information systems (IS) auditor's GREATEST concern when reviewing the contract and associated service level agreement between the organization and vendor should be the provisions for:

options.A: documentation of staff background checks.
options.B: independent audit reports or full audit access.
options.C: reporting the year-to-year incremental cost reductions.
options.D: reporting staff turnover, development or training.

questions.correct_explanation: When the functions of an IT department are outsourced, an information systems (IS) auditor should ensure that a provision is made for independent audit reports that cover all essential areas, or that the outsourcer has full audit access.

wrong_explanations.A: Although it is necessary to document the fact that background checks are performed, this is only one of the provisions that should be in place for audits.
wrong_explanations.C: Financial measures, such as year-to-year incremental cost reductions, are desirable to have in a service level agreement (SLA); however, cost reductions are not as important as the availability of independent audit reports or full audit access.
wrong_explanations.D: An SLA might include human relationship measures, such as resource planning, staff turnover, development or training, but this is not as important as the requirements for independent reports or full audit access by the outsourcing organization.

tips: Trap is A 'staff background checks' — important but periodic; not the audit access concern.
Trap is C 'cost reductions reporting' — financial concern, not assurance concern.
Trap is D 'staff turnover/training' — operational reporting.
Audit access (or independent reports) is the auditor's GREATEST concern with outsourcing. Without it, the auditor cannot verify control effectiveness — defeating the audit's purpose.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor identifies that reports on product profitability produced by an organization's finance and marketing departments give different results. Further investigation reveals that the product definition being used by the two departments is different. What should the I auditor recommend?

options.A: User acceptance testing occurs for all reports before release into production.
options.B: Organizational data governance practices are put in place.
options.C: Standard software tools are used for report development.
options.D: Management signs off on requirements for new reports.

questions.correct_explanation: Data governance directly addresses the problem. An organizationwide approach is needed to achieve effective management of data assets and reporting standards. This includes enforcing standard definitions of data elements, which is part of a data governance initiative.

wrong_explanations.A: User acceptance testing supports the process of ensuring that the system is production ready and satisfies all documented requirements. Recommending that user acceptance testing occur for all reports before release into production does not address the root cause of the problem described.
wrong_explanations.C: The use of standard software tools is one way of achieving uniformity across the different reports and makes support of implemented reports easier. Therefore, recommending standard software tools be used for report development does not address the root cause of the problem described.
wrong_explanations.D: The sign-off by management indicates that they believe all requirements, functions and features have been identified and documented. Recommending that management sign off on requirements for new reports does not address the root cause of the problem described.

tips: Trap is A 'UAT for all reports' — addresses production issues but not data definition consistency.
Trap is C 'standard software tools' — addresses tooling but not the underlying data ownership issue.
Trap is D 'management signs off on requirements' — formality without addressing root cause.
Different departments using different product definitions = data governance failure. Root cause: no enterprise data governance enforcing common definitions. Fix the governance, not the symptoms.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST supports the prioritization of new IT projects?

options.A: Internal control self-assessment (CSA)
options.B: Information systems (IS) audit
options.C: Investment portfolio analysis
options.D: Business risk assessment

questions.correct_explanation: It is most desirable to conduct an investment portfolio analysis, which not only presents a clear focus on investment strategy but also provides the rationale for terminating nonperforming IT projects.

wrong_explanations.A: Internal control self-assessment (CSA) may highlight noncompliance with the current policy but may not necessarily be the best source for driving the prioritization of IT projects.
wrong_explanations.B: Like internal CSA, information systems (IS) audits are mostly a detective control and may provide only part of the picture for the prioritization of IT projects.
wrong_explanations.D: Business risk analysis is part of the investment portfolio analysis but, by itself, is not the best method for prioritizing new IT projects.

tips: Trap is A 'CSA' — control monitoring, not project prioritization.
Trap is B 'IS audit' — assurance activity, not prioritization tool.
Trap is D 'business risk assessment' — input to portfolio analysis but not the full prioritization.
Investment portfolio analysis enables direct comparison: cost, benefit, risk, alignment. Each project earns or loses its place based on portfolio-relative merit.

questions.question: Which of the following is the MOST important information systems (IS) audit consideration when an organization outsources a customer credit review system to a third-party service provider? The provider:

options.A: claims to meet or exceed industry security standards.
options.B: agrees to be subject to external security reviews.
options.C: has a good market reputation for service and experience.
options.D: complies with security policies of the organization.

questions.correct_explanation: An independent security review of an outsourcing vendor is critical because customer credit information will be kept with the vendor.

wrong_explanations.A: Compliance with security standards is important, but there is no way to verify or prove that is the case without an independent review.
wrong_explanations.C: Although long experience in business and a good reputation is an important factor in assessing service quality, the business cannot outsource to a provider whose security control is weak.
wrong_explanations.D: Compliance with organizational security policies is important, but there is no way to verify or prove that that is the case without an independent review.

tips: Trap is A 'claims to meet standards' — claims aren't verification.
Trap is C 'good market reputation' — reputation lags actual current practice.
Trap is D 'complies with org security policies' — claim, needs verification.
External security review = independent verification of controls. With customer credit data, the auditor needs OBJECTIVE assurance, not vendor claims.

questions.question: After the merger of two organizations, multiple self-developed legacy applications from both organizations are to be replaced by a new common platform. Which of the following is the GREATEST risk?

options.A: Project management and progress reporting are combined in a project management office that is driven by external consultants.
options.B: The replacement effort consists of several independent projects without integrating the resource allocation in a portfolio management approach.
options.C: The resources of each of the organizations are inefficiently allocated while they are being familiarized with the other organization's legacy systems.
options.D: The new platform will force the business areas of both organizations to change their work processes, which will result in extensive training needs.

questions.correct_explanation: The efforts should be consolidated to ensure alignment with the overall strategy of the postmerger organization. If resource allocation is not centralized, the separate projects are at risk of overestimating the availability of key knowledge resources for the in-house-developed legacy applications.

wrong_explanations.A: In postmerger integration programs, it is common to form project management offices ( often staffed with external experts) to ensure standardized and comparable information levels in the planning and reporting structures, and to centralize dependencies of project deliverables or resources.
wrong_explanations.C: The development of new integrated systems can require some knowledge of the legacy systems to gain an understanding of each business process.
wrong_explanations.D: In most cases, mergers result in application changes and, thus, in training needs as organizations and processes change to leverage the intended synergy effects of the merger.

tips: Trap is A 'PMO with external consultants' — staffing model, manageable.
Trap is C 'inefficient resource allocation during familiarization' — temporary, expected during integration.
Trap is D 'business process change creates training need' — manageable change management issue.

Multiple independent merger projects without portfolio coordination = duplicated effort, contradictory architectures, missed dependencies. Resource conflicts and architectural drift are unavoidable without portfolio integration.

questions.question: During an audit, an information systems (IS) auditor notices that the IT department of a medium-sized organization has no separate risk management function, and the organization's operational risk documentation only contains a few broadly described types of IT risk. What is the MOST appropriate recommendation in this situation?

options.A: Create an IT risk management department and establish an IT risk framework with the aid of external risk management experts.
options.B: Use common industry standard aids to divide the existing risk documentation into several individual types of risk, which will be easier to handle.
options.C: No recommendation is necessary because the current approach is appropriate for a medium-sized organization.
options.D: Establish regular IT risk management meetings to identify and assess risk and create a mitigation plan as input to the organization's risk management.

questions.correct_explanation: Establishing regular IT risk management meetings is the best way to identify and assess IT-related risk in a medium-sized organization, to address responsibilities with the respective management and to keep the risk register and mitigation plans up to date.

wrong_explanations.A: A medium-sized organization does not normally have a separate IT risk management department due to limited resources. Moreover, the IT risk can usually be managed without the assistance of external experts.
wrong_explanations.B: Although common risk may be covered by industry standards, they cannot address the specific situation of an organization. Individual types of risk will not be discovered without a detailed assessment from within the organization. Splitting the one risk position into several is not sufficient to manage IT risk.
wrong_explanations.C: The auditor should recommend a formal IT risk management effort because a few broadly described types of IT risk contained in the operational risk documentation are insufficient. The failure to demonstrate responsible IT risk management may be a liability for the organization.

tips: Trap is A 'create department + external experts' — overkill for medium org; expensive and slow.
Trap is B 'use industry standards to subdivide existing risk' — administrative cleanup, doesn't add real risk management practice.
Trap is C 'no recommendation needed' — neglects the gap; risk management is essential.
For medium orgs, regular risk management meetings provide the right scale: existing IT staff identify and assess risk regularly, feeding into broader org risk management. Right-sized practice.

questions.question: Overall quantitative business risk for a particular threat can be expressed as:

options.A: a product of the likelihood and magnitude of the impact if a threat successfully exploits a vulnerability.
options.B: the magnitude of the impact if a threat source successfully exploits the vulnerability.
options.C: the likelihood of a given threat source exploiting a given vulnerability.
options.D: the collective judgment of the risk assessment team.

questions.correct_explanation: Quantitative risk analysis methods use numeric values to describe the likelihood and impacts of risk. Thus, the overall business risk can be expressed as the likelihood of the occurrence and magnitude of the impact when a threat exploits a vulnerability and provides the best measure of the risk to an asset.

wrong_explanations.B: A threat source is the intent and method targeted at the intentional exploitation of a vulnerability or a situation and method that may accidentally trigger a vulnerability. A threat is an event or situation that has the potential for causing undesirable consequences or impact. The calculation of risk must consider impact and likelihood of a threat (not a threat source) exploiting a vulnerability.
wrong_explanations.C: The likelihood and impact of a threat (not a threat source) needs to be considered when determining business risk, not just the likelihood.
wrong_explanations.D: The collective judgment of the risk assessment team is a part of qualitative risk assessment but must be combined with calculations of the impact on the business to determine overall risk.

tips: Trap is B 'magnitude of impact only' — half the equation; without likelihood, you can't prioritize.
Trap is C 'likelihood only' — other half; without impact, you can't justify resources.
Trap is D 'collective judgment' — qualitative assessment style; the question asks for QUANTITATIVE.
Quantitative risk = likelihood × impact. Both factors must be estimated numerically. The product gives the dollar-equivalent risk for prioritization.

questions.question: While conducting an audit of a service provider for a government program involving confidential information, an information systems (IS) auditor noted that the service provider delegated a part of the IS work to another subcontractor. Which of the following provides the MOST assurance that the requirements for protecting confidentiality of information are met?

options.A: Monthly committee meetings include the subcontractor's IS manager.
options.B: Management reviews weekly reports from the subcontractor.
options.C: Permission is obtained from the government agent regarding the contract.
options.D: Periodic independent audits are performed of the work delegated to the subcontractor.

questions.correct_explanation: Periodic independent audits provide reasonable assurance that the requirements for protecting confidentiality of information are not compromised.

wrong_explanations.A: Regular committee meetings are a good monitoring tool for delegated operations; however, independent reviews provide better assurance.
wrong_explanations.B: Management should not rely only on self-reported information from the subcontractor.
wrong_explanations.C: Obtaining permission from the government agent is not related to ensuring the confidentiality of information.

tips: Trap is A 'committee meetings include sub-IS manager' — communication mechanism, doesn't verify controls.
Trap is B 'management reviews weekly reports' — vendor self-reports, subject to bias.
Trap is C 'permission from gov agent' — legal/contractual concern, not assurance of control effectiveness.
Periodic INDEPENDENT audit of the subcontractor is the only objective verification of confidentiality control effectiveness — when government data is involved, this rigor is essential.

questions.question: During an audit, which of the following situations are MOST concerning for an organization that significantly outsources information systems (IS) processing to a private network?

options.A: The contract does not contain a right-to-audit clause for the third party.
options.B: The contract was not reviewed by an information security subject matter expert prior to signing.
options.C: The IS outsourcing guidelines are not approved by the board of directors.
options.D: There is a lack of well-defined IS performance evaluation procedures.

questions.correct_explanation: In the case of outsourcing to a private network, the organization should ensure that the third party has a minimum set of IT security controls in place and that they are operating effectively. The absence of a right-to-audit clause in the contract impacts the information systems (IS) auditor's ability to perform the IS audit. Hence, the IS auditor is most concerned with such a situation.

wrong_explanations.B: Having an information security subject matter expert review a contract is a good practice, but it is not a requirement in all industries.
wrong_explanations.C: Approval of the IS outsourcing guidelines by the board is a good practice of governance, and lack of approval is an audit issue. However, it does not impact the IS auditor's ability to perform the IS audit.
wrong_explanations.D: Lack of well-defined procedures does not enable objective evaluation of IS performance and is an audit issue. However, it does not result in major risk or repercussions and does not impact the IS auditor's ability to perform an IS audit.

tips: Trap is B 'no infosec SME review pre-signing' — concern but post-signing audit access can compensate.
Trap is C 'guidelines not approved by board' — governance gap, but doesn't eliminate audit ability.
Trap is D 'no performance evaluation procedures' — operational gap, addressable.
Right-to-audit clause is the auditor's foundational tool for outsourced services. Without it, the auditor has no contractual basis to verify controls — the audit becomes impossible.

questions.question: The MOST important element for the effective design of an information security policy is the:

options.A: threat landscape.
options.B: prior security incidents.
options.C: emerging technologies.
options.D: enterprise risk appetite.

questions.correct_explanation: The risk appetite is the amount of risk on a broad level that an entity is willing to accept in pursuit of its mission to meet its strategic objectives. The purpose of the information security policy is to manage information risk to an acceptable level, so that the policy is principally aligned with the risk appetite.

wrong_explanations.A: The threat landscape is dynamic. It should be considered when developing policy, but it is not the primary factor because policy is not meant to change as often as the threat landscape.
wrong_explanations.B: Prior security incidents may provide insight into the risk appetite statement; however, they are more likely to affect security standards and procedures.
wrong_explanations.C: Emerging technologies are continually evolving. They should be considered when developing policy, but they are not the primary factor because policy is not meant to change as often as technology.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Due to profitability pressure, senior management of an enterprise decided to keep investments in information security at an inadequate level. Which of the following is the BEST recommendation for an information systems (IS) auditor?

options.A: Use cloud providers for low-risk operations.
options.B: Revise compliance enforcement processes.
options.C: Request that senior management accept the risk.
options.D: Postpone low-priority security procedures.

questions.correct_explanation: Senior management determines resource allocations. Having established that the level of security is inadequate, it is imperative that senior management accept the risk resulting from their decisions.

wrong_explanations.A: Cloud computing is cost-effective because costs that are usually directed at purchasing software and hardware are immediately eliminated. However, other costs need to be monitored closely, such as data transfer cost, cloud utilization cost, migration cost and business process reengineering cost. Therefore, the use of cloud providers may or may not provide cost savings or lower risk.
wrong_explanations.B: Compliance enforcement processes that identify high levels of residual risk are working as intended and should not be revised.
wrong_explanations.D: The information systems (IS) auditor should not recommend postponing any procedures. This is a management decision, and management should first accept the risk.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following insurance types provide for a loss arising from fraudulent acts by employees?

options.A: Business interruption
options.B: Fidelity coverage
options.C: Errors and omissions
options.D: Extra expense

questions.correct_explanation: Fidelity insurance covers the loss arising from dishonest or fraudulent acts by employees.

wrong_explanations.A: Business interruption insurance covers the loss of profit due to the disruption in the operations of an organization.
wrong_explanations.C: Errors and omissions insurance provides legal liability protection if the professional practitioner commits an act that results in financial loss to a client.
wrong_explanations.D: Extra expense insurance is designed to cover the extra costs of continuing operations following a disaster/ disruption within an organization.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Errors in audit procedures PRIMARILY impact which type of risk?

options.A: Detection risk
options.B: Inherent risk
options.C: Control risk
options.D: Business risk

questions.correct_explanation: Detection risk is a component of audit risk and is the probability that the audit procedures may fail to detect the existence of a material error or fraud.

wrong_explanations.B: Inherent risk in auditing refers to the risk involved in the nature of business or transaction. It is not affected by human error and is a component of audit risk.
wrong_explanations.C: Control risk is a component of audit risk and is the risk that a material error exists that would not be prevented or detected on a timely basis by the system of internal controls.
wrong_explanations.D: Business risk is a broad category that includes strategic risk, compliance risk, operational risk and reputational risk. It applies to any event or circumstance that has the potential to prevent an enterprise from achieving its business goals or objectives and is not a component of audit risk.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST important to consider when reviewing the classification levels of information assets?

options.A: Potential loss
options.B: Financial cost
options.C: Potential threats
options.D: Cost of insurance

questions.correct_explanation: The best basis for asset classification is an understanding of the total losses that a business may incur if the asset is compromised. Typically, estimating these losses requires a review of criticality and sensitivity beyond financial cost, such as operational and strategic.

wrong_explanations.B: The value of an asset can be greater than its monetary cost, such as impact on reputation and brand.
wrong_explanations.C: The classification of an asset does not change based on potential threats.
wrong_explanations.D: Insurance is obtained based on asset classification.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: Which of the following is of MOST interest to an information systems (IS) auditor who is reviewing an organization's risk strategy?

options.A: All risk is mitigated effectively.
options.B: Residual risk is zero after control implementation.
options.C: All likely risk is identified and ranked.
options.D: The organization uses an established risk framework.

questions.correct_explanation: Risk that is likely to impact the organization should be identified, ranked and documented as part of the risk strategy. Without knowing the risk, there is no risk strategy.

wrong_explanations.A: It is not possible to mitigate all existing risk. However, risk needs to be identified and ranked before effective mitigation can be implemented.
wrong_explanations.B: It is highly unlikely that residual risk would be zero, but it can be reduced. There will always be some level of risk remaining. This is known as residual risk.
wrong_explanations.D: It is not as important to use an established risk framework as it is to identify and rank all likely risk so that it can be addressed.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: An enterprise is looking to obtain cloud hosting services from a cloud vendor with a high level of maturity. Which of the following is MOST important for the auditor to ensure continued alignment with the enterprise's security requirements?

options.A: The vendor provides the latest third-party audit report for verification.
options.B: The vendor provides the latest internal audit report for verification.
options.C: The vendor agrees to implement controls in alignment with the enterprise.
options.D: The vendor agrees to provide annual external audit reports in the contract.

questions.correct_explanation: The only way to ensure that any potential risk is mitigated today and in the future is to include a clause within the contract that the vendor will provide future external audit reports. Without the audit clause, the vendor can choose to forego future audits.

wrong_explanations.A: Although the vendor is providing the most recent third-party audit report for review, there is no agreement contractually that requires the vendor to continue to provide annual reports for verification and review.
wrong_explanations.B: Although the vendor is providing the most recent internal audit report for review, there is no agreement contractually that requires the vendor to continue to provide annual reports for verification and review.
wrong_explanations.C: Without a clause in the contract, an agreement to implement controls does not provide assurance that controls will continue to be implemented in alignment with the enterprise.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is evaluating the IT governance framework of an organization. Which of the following is the GREATEST concern?

options.A: Senior management has limited involvement.
options.B: Return on investment (ROI) is not measured.
options.C: Charge back of IT cost is not consistent.
options.D: Risk appetite is not quantified.

questions.correct_explanation: To ensure that the IT governance framework is effectively in place, senior management must be involved and aware of their roles and responsibilities. Therefore, it is essential to ensure the involvement of senior management when evaluating the soundness of IT governance.

wrong_explanations.B: Managing return on investment (ROI) and thereby creating business value is a part of the objectives in the IT governance framework. Therefore, it is not effective in verifying the soundness of IT governance.
wrong_explanations.C: Introduction of a cost allocation system to facilitate the chargeback of IT cost to the applicable business units is part of the objectives in an IT governance framework. Therefore, it is not effective in verifying the soundness of IT governance.
wrong_explanations.D: Estimation of risk appetite is important; however, at the same time, management should ensure that controls are in place. Therefore, checking only on risk appetite does not verify soundness of IT governance.

tips: GREATEST risk/concern questions reward the option with the broadest blast radius, irreversibility, or regulatory exposure.
Governance questions trace back to the board / audit committee for accountability and to senior management for execution — the IT steering committee operates inside that frame.

questions.question: After an organization completed a threat and vulnerability analysis as part of a risk assessment, the final report suggested that an intrusion prevention system (IPS) should be installed at the main Internet gateways and that all business units should be separated via a proxy firewall. Which of the following is the BEST method to determine whether the controls should be implemented?

options.A: Cost-benefit analysis
options.B: Annual loss expectancy calculation
options.C: Comparison of the cost of the IPS and firewall and the cost of the business systems
options.D: Business impact analysis (BIA)

questions.correct_explanation: In a cost-benefit analysis, the total expected purchase and operational/support costs, and a qualitative value for all actions are weighed against the total expected benefits to choose the best technical, most profitable, least expensive or acceptable risk option.

wrong_explanations.B: The annual loss expectancy is the expected monetary loss that is estimated for an asset over a one-year period. It is a useful calculation that should be included in determining the necessity of controls but is not sufficient alone.
wrong_explanations.C: The cost of the hardware assets should be compared to the total value of the information that the asset protects, including the cost of the systems where the data reside and across which data are transmitted. This comparison is useful as part of the cost-benefit analysis, but not sufficient on its own to determine whether the controls should be implemented.
wrong_explanations.D: A business impact analysis (BIA) predicts the consequences of disruption of a business function and process and gathers information needed to develop recovery strategies. The BIA is only one part of the cost-benefit analysis.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing a contract management process to determine the financial viability of a software vendor for a critical business application. An IS auditor should determine whether the vendor being considered:

options.A: can deliver on the immediate contract.
options.B: is of similar financial standing as the organization.
options.C: has significant financial obligations that can impose liability to the organization.
options.D: can support the organization in the long term.

questions.correct_explanation: The long-term financial viability of a vendor is essential for deriving maximum value for the organization-it is more likely that a financially sound vendor will be in business for a long period of time and thereby more likely to be capable of providing long-term support for the purchased product.

wrong_explanations.A: The capability of the organization to support the enterprise should extend beyond the time of execution of the immediate contract. The objective of a financial evaluation should not be confined to the immediate contract but should be to provide assurance of sustainability over a longer time frame.
wrong_explanations.B: Whether the vendor is of similar financial standing as the purchaser is irrelevant to this review.
wrong_explanations.C: The vendor should not have financial obligations that can impose a liability to the purchaser; the financial obligations are usually from the purchaser to the vendor.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST way to ensure that organizational policies comply with legal requirements?

options.A: Inclusion of a blanket legal statement in each policy
options.B: Periodic review by subject matter experts
options.C: Annual sign-off by senior management on organizational policies
options.D: Policy alignment to the most restrictive regulations

questions.correct_explanation: Periodic review of policies by personnel with specific knowledge of regulatory and legal requirements best ensures that organizational policies are aligned with legal requirements.

wrong_explanations.A: A blanket legal statement in each policy to adhere to all applicable laws and regulations is ineffective because the readers of the policy (internal personnel) will not know which statements are applicable or the specific nature of their requirements. As a result, personnel may lack the knowledge to perform the required activities for legal compliance.
wrong_explanations.C: Annual sign-off by senior management on an organization's policies helps set the tone at the top but does not ensure that the policies comply with regulatory and legal requirements.
wrong_explanations.D: Aligning policies to the most restrictive regulations may create an unacceptable financial burden for the organization. This can then lead to securing minimal risk systems to the same degree as those containing sensitive customer data and other information protected by legislation.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor is reviewing the risk management process. Which of the following is the MOST important consideration during this review?

options.A: Controls are implemented based on cost-benefit analysis.
options.B: The risk management framework is based on global standards.
options.C: The approval process for risk response is in place.
options.D: IT risk is presented in business terms.

questions.correct_explanation: For risk management to be effective, it is necessary to align IT risk with business objectives. This can be done by adopting acceptable terminology that is understood by all, and the best way to achieve this is to present IT risk in business terms.

wrong_explanations.A: Controls to mitigate risk must be implemented based on cost-benefit analysis; however, the cost-benefit analysis is effective only if risk is presented in business terms.
wrong_explanations.B: A risk management framework based on global standards helps in ensuring completeness; however, organizations must adapt it to suit specific business requirements.
wrong_explanations.C: Approvals for risk response come later in the process.

questions.question: An enterprise hosts its data center onsite and has outsourced the management of its key financial applications to a service provider. Which of the following controls BEST ensures that the service provider's employees adhere to the security policies?

options.A: Sign-off is required on the enterprise's security policies for all users.
options.B: An indemnity clause is included in the contract with the service provider.
options.C: Mandatory security awareness training is implemented for all users.
options.D: Security policies should be modified to address compliance by third-party users.

questions.correct_explanation: Having the service provider sign an indemnity clause ensures compliance with the enterprise's security policies, because any violations discovered will lead to a financial liability for the service provider. This will also prompt the enterprise to monitor security violations closely.

wrong_explanations.A: Having users sign off on policies is a good practice; however, this only puts the onus of compliance on the individual user, not on the organization.
wrong_explanations.C: Awareness training is an excellent control but does not ensure that the service provider's employees adhere to policy.
wrong_explanations.D: Modification of security policy does not ensure compliance by users unless the policies are appropriately communicated to users and enforced, and awareness training is provided.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: The corporate IT policy for a call center requires that all users be assigned unique user accounts. On discovering that this is not the case for all current users, what is the MOST appropriate recommendation?

options.A: Have the current configuration approved by operations management.
options.B: Ensure that there is an audit trail for all existing accounts.
options.C: Implement individual user accounts for all staff.
options.D: Amend the IT policy to allow shared accounts.

questions.correct_explanation: Individual user accounts allow for accountability of transactions and should be the most important recommendation, given the current scenario.

wrong_explanations.A: Having the current configuration approved is a recommendation that is not in compliance with the enterprise's own policy and violates good practice.
wrong_explanations.B: Having an audit trail for existing shared accounts does not provide accountability or resolve the problem of noncompliance with policy.
wrong_explanations.D: Shared user accounts do not allow for accountability of transactions and do not reflect good practice.

questions.question: Which of the following reasons BEST describes the purpose of a mandatory vacation policy?

options.A: To ensure that employees are properly cross-trained in multiple functions.
options.B: To improve employee morale.
options.C: To identify potential errors or inconsistencies in business processes.
options.D: To be used as a cost-saving measure.

questions.correct_explanation: Mandatory vacations help uncover potential fraud or inconsistencies. Ensuring that people who have access to sensitive internal controls or processes take a mandatory vacation annually is often a regulatory requirement and, most importantly, a good way to uncover fraud.

wrong_explanations.A: Ensuring that employees are properly cross-trained in multiple functions improves the skills of employees and provides for succession planning but is not the primary purpose of mandatory vacations.
wrong_explanations.B: Improving employee morale helps in reducing employee burnout but is not the primary reason for mandatory vacations.
wrong_explanations.D: Mandatory vacations may or may not be a cost-saving measure, depending on the enterprise, but saving cost is not the primary purpose for the policy.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: The MOST important point of consideration for an information systems (IS) auditor while reviewing an enterprise's project portfolio is that it:

options.A: does not exceed the existing IT budget.
options.B: is aligned with the investment strategy.
options.C: has been approved by the IT steering committee.
options.D: is aligned with the business plan.

questions.correct_explanation: Portfolio management takes a holistic view of an enterprise's overall IT strategy, which, in turn, should be aligned with the business strategy. A business plan provides the justification for each of the projects in the project portfolio, and that is the major consideration for an information systems (IS) auditor.

wrong_explanations.A: Managing the project portfolio within the agreed budget is important, and it should be identified if the project portfolio exceeds the IT budget. However, it is not as critical as ensuring that it is aligned with the business plan.
wrong_explanations.B: Project portfolio alignment has an explicit directive and strategic goal in aligning existing projects to business strategies and ensuring continuous alignment to continue investing in the properly aligned projects and portfolios. Thus, the project portfolio should be aligned with the investment strategy, but it is more important that it is aligned with the business plan.
wrong_explanations.C: Appropriate approval of the project portfolio should be granted. However, not every enterprise has an IT steering committee, and this is not as critical as ensuring that the projects are aligned with the business plan.

tips: MOST/PRIMARY questions ask which option carries the largest impact or coverage — rule out partial or downstream choices.

questions.question: An information systems (IS) auditor observes that an enterprise has outsourced software development to a third-party start-up organization. To ensure that the enterprise's investment in software is protected, which of the following should be recommended by the IS auditor?

options.A: Due diligence should be performed on the software vendor.
options.B: A quarterly audit of the vendor facilities should be performed.
options.C: There should be a source code escrow agreement in place.
options.D: A high penalty clause should be included in the contract.

questions.correct_explanation: The objective of source code escrow is to ensure continued availability of software support and maintenance. Thus, it is primarily recommended to help protect the enterprise's investment in software, because the source code will be available through a trusted third party and can be retrieved if the start-up vendor goes out of business.

wrong_explanations.A: Vendor due diligence is the way in which organizations vet their vendors to spot potential red flags, before entering a contractual relationship. Although due diligence is a good practice, it does not ensure availability of the source code in the event of vendor failure.
wrong_explanations.B: A quarterly audit of vendor facilities is a good practice to continuously evaluate the vendor, but it does not ensure availability of the source code in the event of failure of the start-up vendor.
wrong_explanations.D: A penalty clause imposes a fine on a guilty party for breaching contractual terms. Although it is good practice to include it in the contract, it does not provide protection or ensure availability of the source code in the event of vendor bankruptcy.

tips: ISACA's BEST answer balances control effectiveness, risk reduction, and auditor independence — eliminate options that compromise any of these.

questions.question: Enterprise risk appetite is BEST established by:

wrong_explanations.B: Security management covers all aspects of protecting an organization's assets, including computers, people, buildings and other assets, against risk. The security management team is therefore concerned with managing the security posture but not with determining the posture.
wrong_explanations.C: The primary purpose of the audit committee is to provide oversight of the financial reporting process, the audit process, the company's system of internal controls and compliance with laws and regulations. The audit committee is not responsible for setting the risk tolerance or appetite of the enterprise.

questions.question: A financial services enterprise has a small IT department, and individuals perform more than one role. Which of the following practices represents the GREATEST risk?

options.A: The developers promote code into the production environment.
options.B: The business analyst writes the requirements and performs functional testing.
options.C: The IT manager also performs systems administration.
options.D: The database administrator (DBA) also performs data backups.

questions.correct_explanation: Developers with access to the production environment may run unauthorized code or migrate untested code to production resulting in system unavailability.

wrong_explanations.B: In situations in which there is no dedicated testing group, the business analyst is often the one to perform testing because the analyst has detailed knowledge of how the system must function because of writing the requirements.
wrong_explanations.C: It is acceptable in a small team for the IT manager to perform system administration, if the manager does not also develop code.

questions.question: A financial enterprise has had difficulties establishing clear responsibilities between its IT strategy committee and its IT steering committee. Which of the following responsibilities would MOST likely be assigned to its IT steering committee?

options.B: Aligning IT to business objectives
